title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. N_{1,1} is the arithmetic fundamental group of the moduli stack M_{1,1} over Q. It is an extension 1 → T̂_{1,1}^+ ≅ SL(2,Z)^∧ → N_{1,1} → Γ_Q → 1. The target homomorphism (21), N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ), is the monodromy representation on the Tate module of the universal elliptic curve. Its determinant is the cyclotomic character χ. Grothendieck's question is how much of (21) can be recovered purely group-theoretically from the extension N_{1,1}, in an anabelian spirit.

Previous page. Conjugation gives N_{1,1} → Aut(SL(2,Z)^∧), which descends to Aut(SL(2,Ẑ)) via the congruence quotient. Conjugation by GL(2,Ẑ) on SL(2,Ẑ) has kernel exactly the scalars Ẑ^*. This yields an embedding GP(1,Ẑ) := GL(2,Ẑ)/Ẑ^* = PGL(2,Ẑ) ↪ Aut(SL(2,Ẑ)), and (24) factors through it.

This page, step 1. One obtains (27), φ: N_{1,1} → PGL(2,Ẑ). This is weaker than (21) because the scalar part is lost.

Step 2. To recover more, consider (28), GL(2,Ẑ) → PGL(2,Ẑ) × Ẑ^*, u ↦ (ū, det u).
- Its kernel is the set of scalars λ with λ² = 1, i.e. (29): ₂Ẑ^* = ∏_p {±1} ≅ (Z/2)^P. For p = 2, the torsion of Z_2^* is also {±1}.
- Its image is the fibre product PGL(2,Ẑ) ×_{Ẑ^*/Ẑ^{*2}} Ẑ^*. Here the arrow under GP(1,Ẑ) in the manuscript is the 'determinant mod squares' map PGL_2 → Ẑ^*/Ẑ^{*2}.
- Surjectivity onto the fibre product: lift ū to u with det u = dμ², then uμ^{-1} works.
- Hence GL(2,Ẑ)/₂Ẑ^* ≅ PGL(2,Ẑ) ×_{Ẑ^*/Ẑ^{*2}} Ẑ^*.

Step 3. The pair (φ, χ) in (30) lands in this fibre product, which gives (31), ψ: N_{1,1} → GL(2,Ẑ)/₂Ẑ^*. This is (21) known up to the 2-torsion scalars (Z/2)^P.

Next page. ψ factors through N'_{1,1} = N_{1,1}/{±1}. The remaining problem is to lift to GL(2,Ẑ)/{±1} and then pull back the extension by {±1}.

The margin note restates the aim: to construct the extension N_{1,1} (by Γ̂_{1,1}^+) from the extension N'_{1,1}.
errors: The factorization of (30) through the image of (28) requires det(φ(u)) ≡ χ(u) mod squares. As written this is justified only by knowing that (21) exists: φ = ρ̄ and χ = det ρ. Grothendieck asserts it ('on trouve') without an intrinsic argument, so as a purely group-theoretic reconstruction from the extension it is a gap. As a statement about the true representation it is correct.

Aut_loc must be read as genuine automorphisms (conjugation action), not outer automorphisms. Modulo inner automorphisms, the image of SL(2,Ẑ)·Ẑ^* would die, and PGL(2,Ẑ) would not inject into Out(SL(2,Ẑ)).
Minor: the transcription of the previous and next pages writes GL(1,Ẑ)/Ẑ^* where GP(1,Ẑ) ≅ GL(2,Ẑ)/Ẑ^* is meant.

ideas.what: Recovering the Tate-module representation of the universal elliptic curve, up to scalars, from the conjugation action in the arithmetic fundamental group of M_{1,1} via its congruence quotient
ideas.modern_name: Galois/monodromy representation on π_1 of M_{1,1}; projectivized Tate module representation from outer action
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Tate module of the universal elliptic curve); arithmetic π_1(M_{1,1}) studied by Ihara, Nakamura, Matsumoto et al.
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the Teichmüller tower and M_{1,1}, but not this specific computation

ideas.what: GL(2,Ẑ)/(2-torsion scalars) ≅ PGL(2,Ẑ) ×_{Ẑ^*/Ẑ^{*2}} Ẑ^*, with kernel ₂Ẑ^* ≅ (Z/2)^P
ideas.modern_name: fibre-product description of GL_2 modulo ±1 scalars

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine group-theoretic bookkeeping toward reconstructing a well-known representation (the Tate module of the universal elliptic curve) from the arithmetic π_1 of M_{1,1}. The anabelian motivation is familiar from Esquisse and the later literature.
transcription_corrections: Margin: 'cat.' should read 'ext.' (extension); the same misreading 'l'cat.' occurs on the next page. The margin reads roughly 'i.e. une construction de N_{1,1} [l'ext.] par l'ext. N'_{1,1} de Γ_Q par Γ̂_{1,1}^+' rather than referring to Π_{1,1}.
Under GP(1,Ẑ) in (28), the downward arrow to Ẑ^*/Ẑ^{*2} denotes the determinant-mod-squares map (defining the fibre product), not an equality.
In (30) and (31) the source N_{1,1} is written over a crossed-out symbol; the source is N_{1,1}.
